summary: Round 2 verification of M4.2 (CommitLog moved ingest -> sequencer). All three round-1 minors are fixed and nothing regressed. Verified mechanically: (a) pure-move property holds for BOTH files -- `git show HEAD:ingest/.../CommitLog.java` vs `git show :sequencer/.../CommitLog.java` diffs in the package line only, same for CommitLogTest (191 lines in, 191 out); no member visibility widened, keyFor/logPrefix stay package-private and their only caller moved with them. (b) The seventh reference is qualified at IntervalPutRateTest:35 and a tree-wide grep for `{@link CommitLog}`, `@see CommitLog` and `binjava.ingest.CommitLog` across java/md/kts/py/sh/txt/json finds no remaining dangling reference; the five other surviving textual mentions (CommitDeltaTest, BulkService, BulkEndpointTest, ConditionalWriteConformance, FakeSequencer) are prose or method names, not links. (c) Import order is correct in all three files -- SearchableIT:17, ShardFanOutIT:15, EndToEndTest:19 -- and `./gradlew :plugin:compileClusterTestJava` exits 0, which matters because check-module runs `:plugin:build` and clusterTest is a separate JvmTestSuite outside `check`, so nothing else compiles those two files. (d) `git status --porcelain` shows no unstaged content and `git diff` is empty; the staged diff hashes to the packet's sha; CommitLog.commit's success branch still calls apply(delta) and the file is byte-identical to HEAD modulo the package line, so no mutation survived. CommitLog.java's mtime (08:22:50) postdates the suite run (08:22:35), which looked like a mutation-after-test risk, but `./gradlew :sequencer:test :ingest:test :plugin:test` reports 33/33 UP-TO-DATE against the current sources -- Gradle's input hashing proves the recorded run used exactly today's bytes. (e) Suite: 432 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors across all eight modules; ingest 84, sequencer 26, and TEST-binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest.xml carries all 9 methods green. `GATE_SCOPE=full ./scripts/check-module.sh` re-run: ok, 8 modules, rule5 tested 4, rule2 tested 2 -- exactly the backlog claim. (f) M0.53 is accurate line by line against scripts/test_integrity.py: `git diff --cached --name-only` emits only sequencer/.../CommitLogTest.java, `git show HEAD:<destination>` exits 128 so `before` is None and the loop takes `continue  # new test file: nothing to weaken`, and the source path never enters `paths`; tdd_scan.py:38-39 sets the same `before_ref='HEAD:'`, so both halves go blind on the same input. Distinct from M0.17 (composed annotations, java_tests.py) and M0.52 (task_for source-set mapping). Recording rather than fixing is the right call here: a scanner fix inside this commit would break one-task-one-commit and destroy the pure-move property the task exists to demonstrate, and the risk F1 protects against is independently discharged for THIS commit by the byte-identity above. (g) Cost lens: zero effect on object-store request rate. CommitLog's bytes are unchanged, so its one putIfAbsent per commit and its recovery-only LIST are untouched; the only build change is `testImplementation(project(":binstore-backends"))`, test-only and mirroring ingest's identical line, and CountingBinStore comes from binstore-spi/main so the production surface stays binstore-spi + format as architecture.md:35 requires. (h) The backlog row's claims all check out: architecture.md:35 does assign the write-once commit log to `sequencer`; ingest's `api(project(":sequencer"))` predates this commit at HEAD so no cycle is introduced; all 9 red records exist under binjava.sequencer.CommitLogTest#* dated 2026-09-03 08:16-08:17 alongside the M1.10 originals under the old names. No findings.
